answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like a garden in a dune: every identity must tend a small public plot of shared work through one full slow season before it can transact, and each season's chores are timed to a comet-like orbit that no payment can shorten. A faker who plants a hundred plots still has to wait out a hundred separate seasons, and each season's work is checked by neighbors who have already finished their own, so the cost multiplies with every fake while honest agents keep the single garden they already grew.
